title: The Wizard of Oz
author: L. Frank Baum
ru: Смерч уносит девочку Дороти в волшебную страну Оз, и она с новыми друзьями идёт к Волшебнику, чтобы вернуться домой.

chapters.title: Chapter 1. The Cyclone
chapters.text:
Dorothy lived in Kansas, in the middle of the great grey prairie. She lived with her Uncle Henry and her Aunt Em. Uncle Henry was a farmer. Their house was very small. It had only one room, and under the floor there was a small cellar. It was a cyclone cellar. When the big winds came, the family went down into it.

Everything in Kansas was grey. The grass was grey, the house was grey, and Uncle Henry and Aunt Em were grey and tired too. They never laughed. But Dorothy laughed a lot, because she had a little black dog. His name was Toto. He had long silky hair and small black eyes, and he played with Dorothy all day.

One day, Uncle Henry looked at the sky. It was greyer than usual. The wind was getting stronger.

“There's a cyclone coming, Em,” he said. “I'm going to look after the animals.”

Aunt Em ran to the door. “Quick, Dorothy!” she shouted. “Run to the cellar!”

But Toto was afraid. He jumped out of Dorothy's arms and hid under the bed. Dorothy ran after him. Aunt Em went down into the cellar. Dorothy caught Toto, but it was too late.

The house shook, and then something very strange happened. The house went round two or three times and rose slowly into the air. It was in the centre of the cyclone, and the wind carried it higher and higher.

It was very dark, and the wind was very loud. At first Dorothy was afraid. But hours passed, and nothing bad happened. At last, she lay down on her bed with Toto, closed her eyes and fell asleep.

chapters.title: Chapter 2. The Munchkins
chapters.text:
Dorothy woke up because of a sudden bump. The house was not moving now. Sunshine was coming in through the window. She ran to the door with Toto and opened it.

She cried out in surprise. The country was beautiful! There were green trees, bright flowers and birds with colourful feathers. A small river was running near the house. It was much more beautiful than grey Kansas.

Then some strange people came to her. There were three men and one woman. They were not taller than Dorothy, but they looked older. They wore blue clothes and tall hats with little bells. The woman had a white dress, and her hat had small stars on it.

The woman bowed. “Welcome to the land of the Munchkins, most noble Sorceress,” she said. “Thank you for killing the Wicked Witch of the East. Now the Munchkins are free!”

“But I didn't kill anybody!” said Dorothy.

“Your house did,” said the little old woman. She pointed to the corner of the house. Two feet were coming out from under it. They were wearing silver shoes.

“Oh, no!” said Dorothy. “What are we going to do?”

“Nothing,” said the woman. “She was wicked. I am the Witch of the North, and I am a good witch.”

Then the feet of the dead witch disappeared. Only the silver shoes were there. The good Witch gave them to Dorothy.

“I want to go home to Kansas,” said Dorothy. “Can you help me?”

The Witch shook her head. “Go to the Emerald City. The great Wizard of Oz lives there. Maybe he can help you. Follow the road of yellow brick.”

She kissed Dorothy on the forehead. The kiss left a round, shining mark. “Nobody can hurt you now,” she said.

chapters.title: Chapter 3. The Scarecrow
chapters.text:
Dorothy put on the silver shoes. They fitted her perfectly. Then she took a basket with some bread and started walking on the yellow brick road with Toto.

The road was long, but the day was sunny. The Munchkins were kind to her, and at night she slept in the house of a rich Munchkin.

The next day she stopped near a big cornfield. A Scarecrow was standing on a pole in the field. His head was a small bag of straw with a painted face. He wore an old blue hat and old blue clothes. Dorothy looked at him, and suddenly one of his eyes winked at her!

“Good day,” said the Scarecrow in a quiet voice.

“Can you speak?” asked Dorothy in surprise.

“Of course,” he answered. “How do you do? I'm not feeling very well. It's boring on this pole, day and night. Can you help me down?”

Dorothy lifted him off the pole. He was very light, because he was full of straw.

“Thank you very much,” he said. “I feel like a new man. Who are you, and where are you going?”

“My name is Dorothy, and I'm going to the Emerald City. I want to ask the great Oz to send me back to Kansas.”

“Do you think Oz can give me some brains?” asked the Scarecrow. “My head is full of straw. I don't know anything.”

“I don't know,” said Dorothy. “But you can come with me.”

“Thank you,” he said. “I don't want people to call me a fool.”

So they walked together. The Scarecrow often fell into holes in the road, but it didn't hurt him. He only laughed and stood up again.

chapters.title: Chapter 4. The Tin Woodman
chapters.text:
That night Dorothy and the Scarecrow slept in a small empty house in the forest. In the morning, Dorothy went to look for water. Suddenly she heard a deep groan.

Near the trees, there was a man made of tin. He was holding an axe high in the air, but he was not moving at all.

“Did you groan?” asked Dorothy.

“Yes,” answered the Tin Man. “I did. I'm standing like this for more than a year. Please get the oil can from my little house and oil my joints. They are rusty, and I can't move them.”

Dorothy ran and got the oil can. She oiled his neck, his arms and his legs. Slowly, the Tin Man put down his axe.

“Thank you,” he said. “You saved my life. Why are you here?”

“We're going to the Emerald City to see the great Oz,” said Dorothy.

“Why do you want to see Oz?” he asked.

“I want to go home to Kansas, and the Scarecrow wants some brains.”

The Tin Woodman thought for a moment. “Do you think Oz can give me a heart?”

He told them his story. Once he was a real man, a woodman. He loved a beautiful Munchkin girl. But a wicked witch didn't want them to marry. She put a spell on his axe, and it cut his arms, legs and body. Every time, a kind tinsmith made him a new tin part. But he had no heart now, so he couldn't love the girl any more.

“Brains are not the best thing in the world,” he said. “I think a heart is more important.”

“I think brains are more important,” said the Scarecrow. “A fool doesn't know what to do with a heart.”

Dorothy didn't know which of her two friends was right. But she was happy to have them both.

chapters.title: Chapter 5. The Cowardly Lion
chapters.text:
The yellow brick road went into a deep, dark forest. There were strange sounds among the trees. Suddenly, a terrible roar came from the forest. A big Lion jumped onto the road.

He hit the Scarecrow with his paw, and the Scarecrow fell on the ground. Then he hit the Tin Woodman, and the Tin Woodman fell too. Then the Lion opened his big mouth and ran to Toto.

Dorothy was afraid, but she ran forward and hit the Lion on the nose. “Don't you bite Toto!” she shouted. “You are a big coward. Only a coward attacks a little dog!”

The Lion put his paw on his nose. “I didn't bite him,” he said sadly.

“No, but you tried,” said Dorothy.

The Lion hung his head. “I know,” he said. “I'm a coward. I was always afraid. All the other animals think a lion is the King of the Beasts. When I roar, everyone runs away. But inside, I'm afraid of everything. I'm very unhappy.”

“That's a big mistake,” said the Scarecrow, standing up. “The King of the Beasts can't be a coward.”

“I know,” said the Lion, and a tear ran down his face. “I have no courage. Do you think Oz can give me some?”

“Of course,” said Dorothy. “He can give brains to the Scarecrow, a heart to the Tin Woodman, and courage to you. Come with us!”

So now there were five friends on the road. On the way, they had many adventures. They crossed a deep river on a raft. The Lion carried them over a big hole. In a field of red poppies, Dorothy, Toto and the Lion fell asleep, because the flowers had a magic smell. The Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman, who didn't breathe, carried them away. At last, they saw a beautiful green light in the sky. It was the Emerald City.

chapters.title: Chapter 6. The Emerald City
chapters.text:
The Emerald City had a high green wall around it. At the gate there was a little man, the Guardian of the Gate. He was dressed in green from head to foot.

“You want to see the great Oz?” he said in surprise. “Nobody sees him! He is powerful and terrible. But you are wearing the silver shoes, so maybe he can see you.”

He gave them green glasses. “Everyone must wear these in the city,” he said. “The city is so bright that it can make you blind.”

Inside, everything was green: the houses, the streets, the windows, even the sky. The people wore green clothes and had greenish skin. They were happy.

The Wizard saw the friends one by one. To Dorothy he was a big head without a body. To the Scarecrow he was a lovely lady. To the Tin Woodman he was a terrible beast. To the Lion he was a ball of fire. But he said the same thing to all of them.

“I help nobody for nothing,” said Oz. “In the land of the West, there lives a Wicked Witch. She is the most wicked witch in all of Oz. Kill her, and then I'm going to give you what you want.”

“But I can't kill anybody!” said Dorothy, and she started to cry.

“That is my answer,” said Oz. “Go away and come back after her death.”

The friends were very sad. But they had no choice. The next morning, the Guardian of the Gate took their green glasses back.

“Which road goes to the Wicked Witch of the West?” asked Dorothy.

“There is no road,” he answered. “Nobody wants to go there. Just walk to the west, where the sun goes down. She's going to find you.”

chapters.title: Chapter 7. The Wicked Witch of the West
chapters.text:
The Wicked Witch of the West had only one eye, but it was as powerful as a telescope. She saw the friends when they were still far away. She was very angry.

First she sent wolves, then crows, then black bees. But the Tin Woodman fought the wolves with his axe, the Scarecrow caught the crows, and the bees broke their stings on the Tin Woodman. Then the Witch used her Golden Cap. With the cap, she could call the Winged Monkeys three times.

The Winged Monkeys flew to the friends. They dropped the Tin Woodman on some rocks, and he was badly broken. They took the straw out of the Scarecrow's clothes. They tied up the Lion and carried him to the Witch's castle. But they didn't hurt Dorothy, because she had the mark of the good Witch's kiss on her forehead.

The Witch saw the silver shoes on Dorothy's feet and wanted them very much. They had great magic. Dorothy became her servant. She cleaned the kitchen every day. The Lion stayed in the yard. He refused to work for the Witch, and every night Dorothy brought him food.

One day, the Witch played a trick. Dorothy fell over an invisible iron bar, and one silver shoe came off. The Witch took it quickly.

“Give me my shoe!” shouted Dorothy.

“It's my shoe now,” laughed the Witch. “And soon I'm going to take the other one too.”

Dorothy was very angry. She picked up a bucket of water and threw it over the Witch.

At once the Witch screamed. “Look what you've done! I'm melting!” In a few minutes, she was only a brown puddle on the floor.

Dorothy took her shoe back. The Lion was free. The Winkies, the Witch's yellow servants, were free too. They helped to repair the Tin Woodman and fill the Scarecrow with new straw.

chapters.title: Chapter 8. The Way Home
chapters.text:
The friends went back to the Emerald City. This time the Wizard was not a head, a lady, a beast or a ball of fire. When Toto knocked over a screen in the corner, they saw a little old man with a bald head.

“Who are you?” asked the Tin Woodman.

“I am Oz, the great and terrible,” said the little man in a shaking voice. “But please don't hurt me. I'm only a common man. I came here from Omaha in a balloon many years ago. The people thought I was a great wizard, and I let them believe it.”

But he kept his promise. He gave the Scarecrow new brains made of bran and pins. He gave the Tin Woodman a silk heart filled with sawdust. He gave the Lion a green drink for courage. They were all very happy. In fact, they had these things all the time.

Oz made a new balloon to take Dorothy home. But at the last minute Toto ran away, Dorothy ran after him, and the balloon flew away without her.

So the friends travelled south to Glinda, the Good Witch of the South.

“Your silver shoes can carry you anywhere,” Glinda said. “Knock the heels together three times and say where you want to go.”

The Scarecrow became the ruler of the Emerald City. The Tin Woodman became the ruler of the Winkies, and the Lion became King of the forest. Dorothy kissed her friends goodbye, held Toto in her arms and knocked her heels three times.

“Take me home to Aunt Em!”

In a moment she was sitting on the grey prairie in Kansas. Aunt Em was running to her.

“Oh, Aunt Em!” said Dorothy. “I'm so glad to be at home again!”
